segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Alright!

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: We're going to talk for a little while in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Okay.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏛᎬ ᏯᏛᏛᏂ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎤᏃᏪᎸ ᎠᎭᏂ. ᎾᎾ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎤᏍᎪᎸᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᏒᏂ ᎠᎾᏁᏟᏗ
segments.translation: Alright, we are going to talk for a little while. I am going to ask you what they have written here. It is for the Cherokee language to not fade away, they are trying.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: It is barely hanging on.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᎳᏓ ᎮᏂ Ꮩ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᏃᏭ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏭ ᏥᏓᏅᏕᎵᏆ ᏃᎴ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏯᏅᏛᎦᎩ ᎯᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏯᎾᏕᎶᏆ. ᎠᎬᏱᎾ ᏛᎬᏯᏛᏛᏂ ᏙᏕᏣᏙ ᏲᏁᎩ ᎬᏗ
segments.translation: It is going down now. And also the students here might hear something from you talking that they might learn. I am going to ask you first, what is your name in English?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Lillie vann my maiden name Ross.
segments.translation: Lillie vann my maiden name Ross.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ross ok.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: It's Van now.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Oh, ok.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh ok, in Cherokee what's your name?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Sinasdi.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏏᎾᏍᏗ, Ꭳ ok. ᎦᎲ ᏕᏦᎡ ᏏᎾᏍᏗ?
segments.translation: Sinasdi. Oh ok, who named you Sinasdi?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏗ ᎡᏥᏭ ᎠᎮ ᏓᏬᎡ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏗᎾᏓᎸ ᏏᎾᏍᏗ ᏚᏙᎥ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᎠᏯ Ꮓ ᎠᎩᎷᏥᏝ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᏁᎸ
segments.translation: I guess my mom named me. Her sister’s name was Sinasdi. Then she passed away. When I came, she gave me that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꭳ ok yeah. ᎭᏢᏂ ᏣᏕᏁ ᏃᎴ ᎭᎳᎩ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏒᏗᏒ ᏣᏕᏁ?
segments.translation: Oh ok, yeah. Where were you born and what year were you born?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: December 16th is my birthday.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᏗᏩᏅ ᎾᏂ ᏂᏕᏍᏓᎴ santa claus, santa claus Ꭱ ᎾᎠᏅ ᏂᏕᏍᏓᎴ
segments.translation: You and Santa Claus are just a little close. You and Santa Claus are close.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [laughter]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Santa Claus

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Santa Claus

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Isn’t that what they would say?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: [both laugh]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: You really were born close to Christmas, you came to be.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yeah, Christmas.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where did you grow up?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: There just where they call Greasy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Greasy.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: I just grew up there, never anywhere else.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꭳ ok, ᎢᎦ ᏛᎮ ᎤᏛᏁᏟᏴᏓ Ꮓ ᏙᎭ ᏥᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ?
segments.translation: Oh ok, yeah. I guess it's really changed now, ain't it?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳᏛᎮ ᎾᎠ Ꭸ ᏂᏕᏣᏓᎴ ᏥᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᎢᏣᏢᏅᏢ yeah
segments.translation: When you were growing up, did y’all live close together? When you were growing up with your family?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏦᎦᏓᏝᎦ ᏩᏛ ᎪᎮ ᏥᎦ ᎡᎾᎨ ᎮᏂ Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏱᏕ
segments.translation: We were all together. Now days it’s in the woods. Nobody lives there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No? Uhm.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭ Ꭸ ᎭᏓᏅᏖᏍᎬ ᏪᏙᎰ ᎡᏘᏴ ᎯᎠ ᏥᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ ᎭᏗᏍᎪ Ꮓ
segments.translation: There’s not. Do you sometimes think back and say, “This is how it was long time ago”?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: I can just see it when I think about things.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Do you miss it?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎲ ᏩᏩᏚᎵᎰ ᏩᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᏩᏩᏨᏏᏰᏗ ᏗᏪᏙᎳ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎡᎵᏴ ᎠᏩᏂᎩᏍᏓ
segments.translation: Yeah, I want to go back and walk around where I’ve been but it’s a long ways for me to get there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, ok.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: If I wasn’t scared of bears.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [both laugh]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [unclear]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎤᏍᏗᏓᏁ ᏥᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᏗᏣᎦᏴᎵᎨ Ꮟ ᏣᏁᎲ
segments.translation: What was it like when you were growing up? When your parents were still alive?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎸ Ꮫ ᏨᎩᎸᏂᎲ ᎠᎩᏁᎫᏨ ᎣᏏ ᎨᎲ ᏴᏓᎭ ᏃᎴᏂ ᏍᎫ ᏂᎨᏒᏂ
segments.translation: They use to always whip me. I was mean. Sometimes it was alright and then it wasn’t.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Sometimes you acted mean?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ ᏂᎯ ᏂᎮᏂ ᏕᎭᎴᏅᎡ ᏕᎯᎸᏂᎲ ᎥᏬᏎᎰ Ꮫ
segments.translation: Yeah, they would say, you are starting it, whipping them.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Your siblings, how many were there of you all?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: How many siblings did you have?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏣᏁᎵ ᏎᏃ ᎤᏂᎪᎵ ᏃᏩ ᏅᎩ ᎨᎵ ᎤᏂᎪᎵ ᏦᏍᏛᏓᎸ francis ᏚᏙᎥ ᎤᎩᏙᏅ William, William Ross ᏚᏙᎥ ᏐᎢᎾ ᎤᎩᏙ Johnson Ross ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: Eight, but there are less now. There is four less, I think. My sister, her name was Francis and my brother, William, William Ross. There was another brother, Johnson Ross. That one was a preacher.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Was he a singer too?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, I know him that one.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And also…

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Is Tsinsi your brother?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Tsinsi is my sister?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That's it.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎣᎬᏏ ᎢᏛ ᏥᏂᏏ Linda Ꮎ ᏥᎪᏁᎵ ᏚᏙ Linda ᎣᏂ ᎡᎯ ᏑᏏᏂ Sam Beaver
segments.translation: We are alone, Tsinsi and Linda. Tsigoneli is Linda’s name. She was born last. Susie, Sam Beaver...

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Sam Beaver

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏁᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮲ ᏰᎯ ᏍᏊ ᎣᎬᏏᏃᏭ ᏌᏭ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎤᏘᏴ ᏣᎵ ᏚᏙ Charlie, Charlie Ross.
segments.translation: She was married to Sam Beaver, but he passed away. It’s just us now. I got one brother left, his name is Charlie, Charlie Ross.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Charlie Ross, yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: That’s just how many of us are living.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎫ Ꭸ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏗᏣᏓᏛᏂ ᎨᎮ ᎯᎢ?
segments.translation: Were y'all related?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏱᎨᎵ Ᏺ ᏝᎦ? ᎫᏍᏗ ᎢᎾᏓᏛᏂ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏯ ᏝᎭ?
segments.translation: Uh, I don’t think so. I don’t think you and I are related, are we?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Who?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Me and you.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᏍᎩᏂ Ᏺ ᏍᏗᏁᎵ ᏙᎭ Ᏺ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎣᏍᏛᏓᏛᏂ
segments.translation: But me and your husband are related ain't it?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: On your mom’s side, right?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, okay.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: His grandmother’s name was Gane and his grandpa was…

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Daniel.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Daniel.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Daniel.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭴ ᏍᎩ ᎤᎾ ᏗᏝ ᎤᏠᏯ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏚᏙ ᏍᎩᎾ Soldier ᏣᏗ
segments.translation: He’s related to them on that side. His name is Soldier, you’re talking about.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏣᏁᎵ ᏥᏂᏥᎡ ᏗᏥᏲᏟ ᎡᏩ Ꭸ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎢᏥᎮ ᏕᏣᏛᏏᏗᏒ?
segments.translation: What about when there were eight of you children? Did y’all live in a big house growing up?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᏂᎬ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏥᎳᎨᏲ ᏥᎨ ᏲᎦᏂᏢᏂ ᏌᏭᏭᏂ room ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎩᏅ ᏱᎦ porch Ꭲ ᏣᏰᏍᏛᏍᎬ ᎣᎩᏥ ᎤᎾ ᎣᏥᏂᏝᎣ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, we were scattered everywhere on the floor. It was just one room in the summertime. My mom would lay a something on the porch and we would be laying there.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎢᏣᎵᏍᏓᏂᏙᎸᎾ man ᏙᏳ Ꭱ ᎠᏎ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏭᎪᏛ ᎠᎮ ᏱᏥᏅᏗ ᎤᎾᏓᏍᏓᏂᏙᎸ ᏙᎭ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏣᏁᎲ ᎠᏓ ᏗᎪᏗ
segments.translation: What about when y’all ate? Man, I really miss that the most, is the way they use to cook, the ones that lived long time ago, in a wood cook stove.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏳᏍᏗ ᏛᎮ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏥᎩᏍᎨ ᏍᏊ ᏲᎦᎵᏍᏓᏴᏂ ᎠᏑᏍᏗ ᏃᏩᏛᏥᎦ Ꮟ ᎠᏑᏍᏗ ᎠᏬᏢᏂ ᎠᏯ Ꭱ ᏚᏯ Ꮕ ᎦᏚ ᎢᎾ ᎤᏂᏣᎴᏍᏗ ᏥᏓᏃᏎᎰ biscuit ᏎᎷ ᎦᏚ ᎢᎾ ᏭᏩᎬᏛᏃ ᏄᎾ rice ᏍᏊ ᏛᎮ ᎤᏟ ᏱᎦ
segments.translation: We ate anything when we ate. Gravy. Even now I’m full with gravy, beans and bread. Untsilesdi is what they call biscuits and corn bread and the rest was potatoes, rice. That was mostly it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎫᏍᏗ Ꮕ ᎦᎾᏢᏗ ᏧᏂᎾᏝᎥ ᏙᎭ ᏏᏆ, ᏥᏔᎦ, ᎫᏇ ᏳᏓᎭᏂ ᏩᎦ ᏳᎾᏝᎢ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎩᎶ ᏙᎭ
segments.translation: They had some farm animals ain’t it. Hogs, chickens, guineas and sometimes someone would have a cow.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yeah, chickens.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎲ ᏥᏔᎩ ᏛᏲ ᎣᎩᏥ ᏳᏟ Ᏺ ᎣᏥᎩᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏌᎶᎵ ᏕᎲᏂ ᏥᏍᏚᏅ ᎧᏄᏂᏅ ᏗᎦᎬᎵ ᎤᏂᏖᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎮᏩᏛ ᏂᏕᎩ ᏗᎦᏅᎯᏓ ᎤᏁᎦ ᎭᏫᏯ Ꭵ ᏌᎵᎫᎦ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᎦ ᎭᏫᏯ
segments.translation: When our mom killed one, we would eat it, then and squirrels and rabbits too, and frog legs. They are delicious, but they are just this big. The meat is white. I have ate turtle meat too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏍᏊ ᏗᎧᏃᎨᏄᏭ ᏱᎦ meat ᏄᏩᏂ ᎤᏣᏘᎾ Ꮭ ᎫᏇ Ꮕ ᏥᏍᏆ ᏚᏘ ᎢᎾ ᏥᏓᏃᎮᎰ snowbird ᏳᏍᏗᏛ ᏛᎮ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏥᎩᏍᎨ ᎣᎩᏁᎲ
segments.translation: It has meat just on its arms. In other places it don’t and quails and birds and tuti, they call them snowbirds. I guess we ate whatever they gave us.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Snowbird(s).

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: We were eating.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎪᎯᎮᏂ ᏥᎦ ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎰ Ꮎ ᎣᏂ ᏧᎾᏛᏒ ᏂᎬ ᎥᏳᎩᎯ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎢᏛᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎵ
segments.translation: Nowadays I tell them younger ones it’s everywhere there is things to eat,

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Right.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎯᏛ ᎤᏪᏘ ᎯᎡ can ᎦᎵᏢᏛ Ꮲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦ ᏫᏣᏚᎦ Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏘ Ᏼ ᎦᎵᏝᏛᏅ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: This can is old, it’s not good. Nobody knows when it was canned.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No, huh uh.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Well wild onion and polk salad.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Polk salad.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎠᎪᏍᏗ ᎠᎩᏍᏗᏅ ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᎠᏥᎳ ᎠᎹ ᎤᏚᎯᏅ ᎤᎤ
segments.translation: And lettuce, they call it. And watercress, that’s what I like when I eat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Boy.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: That’s the type of stuff of I like to eat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s good things like that.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yeah,

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏦᏥᎦᎭᎷᏍᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎪᎢ ᎤᏗᏝᎦ ᏬᏥᏍᏚᏟᏍᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎠᎹ ᎦᏚ boy ᏍᎩᏛ
segments.translation: We cut it up. Then we pour hot grease on it and salt on top.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Yeah, ᎤᏖᏗ ᎪᎯᏅ ᏥᎦ ᏣᏁᎭ ᎤᎤ ᏯᏅᏗ ᎠᏂᏁᎵᎰ ᎠᎸᎯᏳᏛ ᏛᏟᎶᏟ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎠᏟᎶᏢᏂ ᏂᏣᎸᏫᎬᏛᏂ ᏣᎩᏍᏗᏛ ᏂᏓᎦᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s good. And now days, these ones that are living they will say, “Oooooh!” they don’t like it. “There is going to come a time when you are going to have to eat what you don’t like.” I tell them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What about crawdads?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Crawdads.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏥᏍᏛᏂ yeah, ᏗᎩᎸᏩᎦᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏍᏛᏂ ᎠᏣᏗ Ꭱ ᏫᏓᎩᎸᏩᎦᏓ ᎤᏂᏖᏕ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏣᏗ ᏗᎦᏰᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᏱᎦᏂᎦ ᎠᏂᏐ
segments.translation: Yeah. I liked crawdads too. I like fish. The most fish are good to eat. Others won’t eat it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎤᏟᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏂᏓᎩᎸᏩᎦᏓ Ꮎ ᎤᏩᏴ ᏗᎦᏂᏴᏓ Ꮎ ᏧᎾᏍᏗᏭ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎠᏭ ᏂᏗᎬᏁᎸ ᏎᎷ ᎢᏌ ᏗᎦᏅᎵᏰᏗ ᏍᏓᏯ ᏗᏒᏂᏛᏅ yeah ᎤᏟᎯᏂᏏ ᏥᏍᏛᏂ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᏳᏩᎾᎵᏑ
segments.translation: I like them more from the creek, when you just scrape them like this, with cornmeal on them fried real hard. Yeah, especially if there is a few crawdads mixed in.

segments.translation: Gawlee, man. Yeah.

segments.translation: [phew]

segments.translation: The food was good through time.

segments.translation: I tell them that I'm still hungry for the thing I use to eat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, did y'all plant a garden?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎲ ᎠᏂᏫᏒᏍᎩ Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏥ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏎᎷ ᏧᏛᎴᏅᏗ ᏚᏯ greenbeans, mustard greens ᏒᎩ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏫᏒᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏌᏭ ᎮᏂ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ ᎣᎩᏅᏙᏅ ᎨᎵᏍᎬ Ꭱ ᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸᏒ ᏕᎨᏥᎾᏝᎥ ᏠᎨᏏ ᎠᏂ ᎠᏂᏰᎲᏍᏗᏍᎦ ᎤᎾ ᏩᏁᏙᎲ ᎡᏥ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎠᏯᏅ ᎣᏥᏅ ᏩᎦ Ꭱ ᏙᎬᏓᏓᏁᎸ ᏎᎷ ᎠᏫᏒ ᎤᎤ ᎤᏛᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏂᏏ ᏣᏗ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ ᎠᏯᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏗᏝ Ꮟ ᏛᎾᏕᎳᎰᏎ ᎠᏂᎷᏧ Ꭰ Ꮒ ᏚᎾᎳᏍᎦᏅ ᎤᏛᏅ ᎦᎶᎪᏗ ᎢᏓ ᏙᎦᏕᏏᏙᎰ ᎣᏥᏲᏍᏗᎲ ᏚᎾᎳᏍᎬ ᏗᏂᎦᏩᏍᏕᏒ Ꮕ ᎤᏂᎷᏣᏭᏅ ᎤᎾᏕᎳᎰᏒ
segments.translation: Yes, my mom and dad used to plant a garden: corn, green beans and different things. Mustard greens and onions, they used to plant. One time we made a mistake. I think they went to work. They had jobs in the field planting strawberries. Mom and dada were over there, we were home. We let the cows into the corn patch. Tsinsi said, “Ooooh!” She next to the oldest behind me. “They are going to find out when they get back there. Footprints are there,” she said. We started throwing hoes around to break up the footprints. They had broke the corn off. As soon as they got back, they found out.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Did y'all get scolded again?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᎤᏓᎷᎳᏅᏩᏛ ᏦᎩᎸᏂᏍᏗ. ᎡᏚᏗᎾ ᎡᏥ ᎤᏙᏗ ᏍᎫ ᏧᏫᏒᏅ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᎬᎩᏍᏓ ᎯᏛ ᏱᏗᏂᏓ ᏥᏓᎲ. ᏙᎩᎦᎲ ᏒᎩ ᎣᎩᏲ Ꭴ Ꮒ ᎾᎾ ᎡᏚᏗ ᎤᏫᏒᏅ Ꮎ ᏂᏚᏩᏂᏭ ᎤᏛᏅ ᎤᎾᏭᏛ ᎣᎨᏅᏒ ᎦᎷᏍᏗ ᎦᎵᏎ. ᎠᏬᎯᏳᏒ ᎬᎩᏍᏓ ᎨᎲ ᏫᏥᎷᏴ ᏓᎶᏂᎨᏭᎨᎲ ᎣᏥᏂᏏᏂᏙᎲ ᎢᏯ. ᏢᏂ ᎤᎦᎾᏍᏗ ᏱᎦ ᎠᏗᎰᏛ Ꮮ ᎢᏯ Ꮕ ᎨᎮ ᎬᎩᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏤᎵᏍᎬ ᎦᎬᎻ ᏕᎰ ᏍᎫ ᏗᎩᎸᏩᎩᏗ ᎾᏅ green tomatoes
segments.translation: Yeah, we came close to getting a whipping. My grandpa, my mom’s dad, also had a garden on the creek. There were watermelons this big setting there. We seen them while looking for onions. “Oowee! Look at grandpa’s garden! Look what he has!” they said. And we went right back. I was carrying an axe on my back. I thought it was a watermelon and chopped it. It was just yellow. We were dragging around a punkin! He said, “It’s not sweet.” No, it was a punkin. We thought it was a watermelon. I also like cucumbers and green tomatoes fried real thin.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ah, man.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: "The fried green tomatoes. Ooh!"

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gawlee!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏳᏍᏗᎭ Ꭱ ᏱᏕᏥᎦ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎫᏍᏚᏭ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏄᏠᏯᏍᏛᏂ
segments.translation: I can eat those alone without anything else.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Man [whistle], boy ᎠᏎᎾ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏣᏁ Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏳᎾᏚᎵ
segments.translation: Man [whistle], boy but like you said kids now would not want that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᎾᏫᏛ macdonalds Ꭲ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏳᎾᏚᎵ
segments.translation: They would just want McDonald's or places like that.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏃᏩᏛ ᏥᎦ Ꮟ ᏨᎩᎵᏏ, ᎢᏥᎩᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᏁᏟᏕ ᎮᏂ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎢᏥᎩᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᏕᎳᎰᏍᎩ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦ Ꮲ ᎴᏱᎦ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ. Ꮧ ᎾᎾ ᏓᎳᏥ ᏡᎦ Ꮎ ᎤᏂᏍᎫᏱ ᏧᎾᏙ
segments.translation: That’s it. The grandkids I have now. Eat it, if y’all will try to eat something, you will find out if it’s good or not, I tell them, but they don’t. Dalvtsi trees, those unisguyi that hang there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The acorns.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏕᎦᏕᏍᎬ ᎬᏩᎦᏙᏍᏛ ᏫᏗᎦᏕᎰ ᏕᏥᎩᏍᎬ ᎤᎤ ᎤᏛᏅ ᎠᏪᏥ ᎠᎨᏳᏥ mama Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏚᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏯᎦ Ꮒ Ꮎ ᎠᎩ.
segments.translation: They watch me pick them. I pick them and eat them. My daughter said, “Oooooh, momma, will eat anything! Look what she’s eating!”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏲᏁᎩ ᎬᏗ ᎤᏂᏍᎫᏱ?
segments.translation: What is that in English, unisguyi?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏲᏁᎩ ᎬᏗ ᏞᏍᏕ ᏍᎫ ᏯᏩᏘ. ᎤᏂᏍᎫᏯ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏲᏁᎩ ᎬᏗ Ꮭ ᏱᏣᏘ?
segments.translation: What is that in English? I don’t really know unisguyi. Do you know?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎭᏗ ᏯᏩᏘ Ꮭ ᎮᏂ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏲᏁᎩ ᎬᏗ ᏯᏩᏘ. ᎤᏂᏍᎫᏯ ᏓᏃᏎᎰ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏁᏘᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏂᎦᎾᏍᏗ ᎠᏁᏐ ᎢᎾ Ꮲ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᏍᏗ ᎤᏣᏘᏂ ᏕᏡᎦ ᎤᎾᏛ
segments.translation: I don’t know. I don’t hardly know anything in English. They call them unisguyi. They are good. They are real sweet. Others are not like that are on different trees.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᎾᎾ Ꮕ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ ᎧᏩᏯ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎧᏅᏗ ᏥᎦ Ꭵ Ꭿ ᏃᏩᏥᎦ ᎡᎯ ᎢᏤ ᏢᏍ ᎪᎵ ᎬᏂᏍᎩ, ᎪᎵ ᎬᏂᏍᎩ ᏯᏃᎮᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: What about that one that looks a little bit like huckleberry? It’s green about this time. What do they call it? Ripens in the winter.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Kocheni.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎪᎵ ᎬᏂᏍᎩ ᏣᏛᎦᏅᏍ ᏍᎩᎾ? ᎪᎵ ᎬᏂᏍᎩ
segments.translation: “Kola gvnsgi,” have you heard that? “Ripens in the winter.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I really haven’t.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎧᏩᏯ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎧᏂᏕ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᎧᏩᏯ ᏱᎦ
segments.translation: It looks a little bit like huckleberry, but it’s not huckleberry.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Kolagvnsgi.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Kolagvnsgi.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Kolagvnsgi.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎪᎵ ᎬᏂᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏩᎦ ᏯᏩᏤᎸᏂ ᏱᏓᏩᏁᎶᏁᏂ ᎣᏓᎳ ᎣᏥᎵᏙᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏈᏍᏓ ᏕᏡᎪ ᎤᏙ ᏥᏂᎪ Ꮫ wear ᏂᎬᏁᎰ ᎬᏕᏍᎬ ᏥᎩᏍᎬ ᎤᏖᏗ ᎮᏂ Ꭰ ᎫᏍᏗ. ᎧᏂᎦ Ꮕ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎩᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎧᏂᎦ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏖᏗ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ ᏐᎯᏅ Ꮲ ᏯᏂᏟᎦ ᎤᎾ ᏴᎦᎵᏍᏛᏢᎦ ᏴᎦᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᎦ
segments.translation: Kolagvnsgi. It ripens in the winter. I would act like a cow and go play. We would be all over the mountain. There would be lots of trees on there. I would wear my tongue picking it and eating it. It’s good to eat, and also kanek. I would eat that too. Kanek, it’s good. And if there were hickory nuts on the ground somewhere I would sit there and eat.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Just like squirrel.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏳᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᎨᎲ ᏎᏗ Ꮎ
segments.translation: Yeah, and walnuts.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛᎮ ᏳᏍᏗ Ꮟ ᏥᏂᏙᎯ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏣᎵᏍᏓᏂᏙᎸ
segments.translation: That’s probably why you are still healthy now days, is how you ate.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎲ Ꭴ ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎰᏭᏛ ᏥᎪᏩᏘᏍᎪ ᏭᏛ ᏯᎩᏃᎮᏟᎩᎾ
segments.translation: Yeah, I want it. I can just see it when I talk about it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮕ ᎧᏂᎦ ᏣᏗ ᏍᎩᎾᏅ ᎪᎵ ᎬᏂᏍᎩ ᏃᏭᏍ ᏥᎦ ᎡᎯ ᎢᏤ ᎯᏴ Ꮲ ᏥᎦ?
segments.translation: That kanek, you said it ripens in the winter? Is it green about this time?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᎠᏎᏃ ᎨᏍᏗ ᏳᏗ ᎤᏛᏢᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎪᎵ ᎬᏂᏍᎩ ᎧᏂᎦ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏛᏢᏗ ᏕᏡᎦ ᏕᏥᎪᏩᏘᎰ Ꭵ ᏝᏯᏩᏘ ᏄᏰᏟᏛ ᎠᏓᏢᏗᏍᎬ
segments.translation: Yeah, but it don’t exist. It went away, kolagvnsga. Kanek has went away too. I see the trees, but I don’t know why it went away.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Do they grow on big trees?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎲᎥ ᏅᎡ Ꮕ ᏙᏱ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎾᎠ ᏗᏝ ᏧᎬᏅᎾ ᎧᏩᏯ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎧᏅᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎤᏗ ᎢᏤ ᎧᏩᏯ ᏭᏅ ᏍᎫ ᎡᎵᏍᏓ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏞᏍᏕ ᏱᎦᏅᏍᎦ
segments.translation: Over there, by Beaver Church, the road that goes that way, there is something that looks like huckleberry. It’s green, but it’s not huckleberry. It’s not ripe.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: One of them they called ulotisgi.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: What is it?

segments.translation: Ulotisgi

segments.translation: Ulotisgi

segments.translation: Ulotisgi

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Yeah, ᎯᏩ ᎮᏂ Ꮲ ᏂᎦᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎧᏩᏯ ᎡᎵᏍᏓ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎧᏩᏯ ᎯᎥᏢ ᏂᎦᏙ ᏙᎭ? ᎯᎮᏂ Ᏺ ᎯᏢ ᏂᏕᎦᏘ ᏗᎧᎾᏗ ᎡᏲ ᎯᏢ ᏂᏕᎬᏗ ᏗᎧᎾᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ Ᏺ ᎧᏩᏯ ᎡᎵᏍᏓ ᎢᏤ ᎤᏗ
segments.translation: Yeah, it’s just this tall, just like huckleberry, but huckleberry is just this tall ain’t it. But these are this tall, but the green berries look like huckleberry.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ulotisdi.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎤᎶᏘᏍᏗ ᏲᎶᏘᎦ Ꭸ ᏴᎦ ᏙᎨ? ᎣᏍᏓᏍ ᎠᎩᏍᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᎨ?
segments.translation: Ulotisdi. Will it make you full if you eat it or what? Is that good to eat or what?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ ᎤᏛᏢᏗᏛ ᎤᎪᏗ ᏍᏈᏍᏓ ᎤᏓᏢᏗ Ꮭ ᏰᎯ ᏱᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᏃᏭ.
segments.translation: Yeah, it's went away. A lot has went away. I don’t think it exists anymore.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Yeah ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᏣᏢᏅᏛᏕᎵ ᏣᏛ ᎤᎾ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏙᏱ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎦᏚᏏ
segments.translation: If you ever get time, you know where Beaver Church is, on the mountain?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: The Beaver Church?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏅᏃ ᎣᎾ ᎤᏣᏞᏏ Ꮎ ᏧᎦᏣᏃ ᏍᏆᎳ ᏃᏭ ᏫᎦᏕᏍᏗ ᎯᎤ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏗᏝ ᏅᏃ ᎠᏍᏛ ᎤᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏘ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: If you turn, there is a straight away, then a sharp curve. Just this side there is berries. I don’t know what it is.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Another they call it uthlosinvdi and blackberry.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, blackberry.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏒᏗᏩᎵ Ꮕ ᎤᏠᏳ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᏍᏓ Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᎬᎾ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎥᎩᎳᏩᎦᏓ Ꮫ ᎨᎲ ᎫᏍᏗ ᎠᎩᎩᏍᏗ
segments.translation: And svdewali, it’s the same and you can eat it. I have ate that too. I like to eat things like that.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: boy ᎪᎯᏴ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎦ ᎮᏍᏕ ᎩᎶ ᏯᎦᏔᎭ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎪᏟᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᎩᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏙᎭ? ᎠᏯ Ꮽ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎦ Ꭵ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏘ ᎤᏟᏱᎦ
segments.translation: Now days, boy, nobody know how to recognize those things that are edible, ain’t it. As well as me, I don’t know a whole lot.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏒᏗᏩᎵ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏃᏎᎰ ᎤᏠᏱᏭ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎧᏄᎦᏟ ᎠᎩᏍᏓ
segments.translation: Svdewali, they call it. It's almost like blackberry to eat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Svdewali.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Svdali ... I might be saying ant(s).

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Svduwal(i) Svduwal(i)

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏙᎲ Ᏺ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨ ᏢᏅ ᎤᏟᏱᎦ ᏗᏓᎾᏅ ᎢᏤᏙ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏝᎭ Ꮟ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎢᏥᏩᏘᎮ. Ꮎ ᏗᎨᏣᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᏙᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏅᏛᏁ ᎨᎮ ᎢᏨᎵᏍᏕᏝᏙᏗ?
segments.translation: I might be saying aunt, back then y'all really didn’t go to the store and y'all still found food. What did your parents do to provide for y'all?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: That’s it, you mean for money?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Jim Worsham Ꮫ ᏧᏙᎩᏓ ᏥᏚᏫᏒ ᎠᏂ. ᏧᏔᏂ ᎤᎾ ᏕᎨᏥᎾᏝᎣ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᏰᎲᏍᏗᎲ ᎠᏂᎶᎩᏍᎬᏂ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎤᎾ ᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏒᎯᏰᏅ ᏌᎾᎴ ᏳᎾᎴᏅ ᏒᎯᏰ ᎠᏂᎷᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏕᎨᎬᏈᏴᎡᎲᏂ ᏧᎾᎩᎶᏍᏗ ᎢᎦ
segments.translation: Jim Worsham was the name of the man that had strawberries, planted big strawberries. They worked there planting it and hoeing it. They use to work there all the time. They would start in the morning and come back in the evening from working, and got paid on Fridays.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: So they really found work close to where y'all were.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Just close by.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏩᏘᎮ ᏗᎬᎸᏫᏍᏓᏗ, Ꮎ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏯ ᏥᏗᏥᏁᎵ Ꮎ Bunch Ꭲ ᎦᏚᏏ
segments.translation: Over there, where I lived at Bunch on the mountain. Do you remember long time ago where Daylight used to live, it was a peach orchard.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎭᏅᏛᏗ ᎪᎯᎦ Ꮎ Daylight ᏥᏛᎬᏁᎸ ᏆᏃ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Do you remember where Daylight used to live? It used to be a peach orchard.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: It was a peach orchard,

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Yeah, ᎤᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ ᏙᎭ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾ ᏍᏈᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎦᎸᏫᏍᏓᏗ ᎪᎩ ᏱᎦ
segments.translation: Yeah, it used to be like that a long time ago ain’t it, and there was lots of work there a long time ago.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎥᎲ ᎠᎮᏂ ᎪᎯᏴᏥᎦ Ꮲ ᏱᎦᏛᏩᏘ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ, ᏝᏅ ᏯᏩᏘ
segments.translation: Yes, now days, you can’t find anything like that, I don’t know.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: There ain't nothing there. It’s just fields.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏙᎨ ᎾᏭᎨ ᏣᏂᎪᏕᏍᎪ ᏣᏂᏂᏏᏂᏙ ᏂᎦᏗ roots ᎠᏂᎯᎯ
segments.translation: You think it’s because they are grading it? Dragging it around. They are killing all the roots.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That’s it, ain’t it.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: That’s what I think.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏅᏃ ᎤᏭᏂ ᎣᏍᏛ ᏳᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎧᏄᎦᏟ Ꭰ ᎤᏂᏖᎸᎸᏗ ᎾᏅ Ꮩ ᏥᏚᏙ?
segments.translation: There would be blackberries on side of the road and grapes or, what’s the name of that?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Possum grapes.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That's it.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: possum grapes ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎩ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏘ
segments.translation: Possum grapes, is what they call it in English. I don’t know.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: And plums.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ ᏆᏄᎾᏍᏗ ᎡᎾᎨ ᎠᏁᎯ Ꭰ ᏒᎵ Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏥᎩᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏒᎵ Ꮎ ᎤᏩᏂᏒ ᏩᏂᎨ ᏳᎵᏍᏛᏅ
segments.translation: And plums from the woods. And persimmons. We use to eat persimmons when it ripens and gets soft.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: When they start dropping ain't it.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᎤᏖᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᏍᏗ ᎯᏃ ᏕᏡᎩ ᏃᏩ ᏥᎦ ᏕᏡᎦ Ꮭ ᏳᏗ
segments.translation: It's also good to eat. Even now there are trees, that's not got any berries on it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: It don’t.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: There's nothing.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Things are going away.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah it is.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Like you said a while ago, we have been provided with it.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏂᏓᏗᏍᎬᏄ ᏛᎮ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ Ꭰ Ꭰ ᎠᏛᏢᏗ ᏴᏗ ᏛᎮ ᏙᎭ?
segments.translation: I guess it’s because we don’t use it, it’s just disappearing you could say ain’t it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏙᏳ ᎮᏂ ᎾᏂ ᎨᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᏓᏢᏗᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᎪᏂ ᏣᏗ right there. that’s where ᎤᎾ ᎢᏕᏙ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎦ ᏂᎦᏥᏪᏎᎰᏂ ᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᏤᎵᏍᎪ ᏢᏍ ᏱᏥᎪᏩᏘᎰ ᎦᏥᏲᏎᎰ ᎠᏯ ᎡᏲ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ ᏙᏛᎪᏄᎶᏏ ᏣᏗ
segments.translation: It is really true. Where it says when it’s getting close this are going to disappear with hunger right there that’s where we are at

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: If these stores shut down.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yeah, it's highly likely.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Where are we going to look for something?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏴᏛᏂ Ꮎ computers ᎡᎳᏓ ᏱᏂᏚᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᏂᎬ ᎡᎶᎯ
segments.translation: Like, for instance, if the computers go down in the world?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎠᏪᎵᏎ ᎤᎡ ᎤᎾ ᎠᎹᏯ ᎨᏙᎲ ᎤᎾ bunch Ꭲ ᏗᏝ ᎮᏍᏕ ᏥᏍᏛᏂ ᏱᏗᏥᎪᏩᏘ
segments.translation: I have noticed from going to the creek towards Bunch, I don’t see any crawdads.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᏈᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏱᏣᎳᏍᎬᏍ ᎤᏛ ᎯᎢ ᏱᎾᏅᎵᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: There used to be lots of them. If you just took a step they would do this.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: They would scatter.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮓ ᏛᏲ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᎾᏪᏙᎵ ᎠᎹᏯ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏱᏥᎪᏩᏘ ᏥᏍᏛᏂ
segments.translation: I have been to the creek a few times. I haven’t seen a crawdad.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: They are being stingy with them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I know

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎠᏂ game warden ᏨᎾᏗᏍᎬ ᎠᎩᏍᏗᏅ. ᎲᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏃᏢᏅ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎢᏗᏰᎳ ᎤᎵᏍᏕᏟᏙᏗ ᎤᎬᏩᏟ
segments.translation: Game wardens, they say they crawdads aren't made to be eaten. It’s for the nourishment of the body, the purpose.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: What about medicine? Can you still find things to use?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏅᏬᏘ ᏛᎨᎲ ᎧᎵᏤᏥ ᏥᏄᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁ ᎧᏩᏯ ᎠᏛᏛᏍᎩ ᏂᎨᏒᏂ. ᎤᎵᏑᏯ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏛᏛᏍᎩ ᎧᏩᏯ Ꮲ ᏳᏙ ᏯᏥᎸᏁ ᎠᎮᏂ Ꮲ ᎧᏩᏯ ᏱᎬᏙᏢᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᎾᏍᏕᏟ ᏅᏬᏘ
segments.translation: As for medicine, you know how they have diabetes? There are huckleberry that don’t get berries on it. There is a huckleberry plant mixed in that don’t get berries on it. It will bloom, but it won’t get berries on it. The root from it is medicine.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: We'll I'll be!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎨ Lillie ᏛᎬᏯᏛᏛᏂ ᎩᎶ ᏴᏫ ᎠᏎᏍ ᎠᏥᏁᎸ ᎨᎰ ᏧᏓᏅᏬᏗ ᏙᎨ ᎦᎫᎨ ᎨᎲ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏛᏂ ᏳᏍᏕᎵ
segments.translation: That… Lillie, I’m going to ask you, does a person have to be gifted to be a healer or does it matter who uses it? Can it be helpful?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏗ ᎩᎶ, ᏴᏕᏠᎨ ᏳᏓᏃᏎᎵ ᏴᏕᏠᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎩ ᏛᎮ ᏳᎵᏍᏓᏂᏙᎸ ᎤᏅᏙ ᎠᎮ ᎠᏓᏅᏫᏍᎦ
segments.translation: You can learn if they tell. You can learn. It’s because of that, the healer knows.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎠᏎᎾ ᎢᎳᎦᏯ ᏅᏍᏊ Ꮩ ᎪᎯᏗ ᎬᏙᏗ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎫ ᏥᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᎦ ᏙᎭ
segments.translation: I guess you really have to use faith with that to ain't it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: I mean Ꮩ ᎪᎯᏓ ᎬᏙᏗ ᎦᏣᏍᏕᏟᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: I mean you really have to use faith that it can help you.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎤᏴᏟᏅ ᎤᏂᏂᏱᎲ, ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᏛᏲ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎠᏯ ᎠᏩᏅᏛ ᎨᎲ. ᎩᏔᏯ ᏥᏕᏡᎪ ᏧᏩᏛᎸᏗ ᎠᎵᏝᏛᎾ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏃᏩᎴᏂ ᏒᏂ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏃᏎᎰ ᏍᎩ ᏛᏲ ᏒᏂ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏯ ᎠᏩᏛᎯᏍᏛᏅ. Ꮩ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏯᎯᎵᏙ ᎥᏴᎨ ᎠᎯᎵᏙ ᏳᎾᏛᏂ ᎡᏙᏓ Ꮫ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᏛᏴ ᎤᏯᎴᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ roots ᏒᏂ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎪᏧᏁᎦᏅ ᏗᏓᎨ ᎾᎾ ᏗᎦᏂᏍᏗ ᏧᎦᎾᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᏥᏚᏰᎪ ᏗᎦᏂᏍᏗ ᎧᎾᏑᏠᏩᎾ ᎠᏃᏎᎮᎰ Ꮠ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏍᏆᎸᏴ ᎠᏍᏓ ᏴᎦᎳᏪᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ Ᏼ ᏱᎦ ᏂᏕᎬᏁᎰ ᎠᎹ Ꮕ ᏯᏟᏍᏓ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏌᏭ ᏱᎦᏢᎦ ᏯᎵᏟᏗ ᎤᏖᏗ Ꮲ ᎸᎯᏳ ᎦᏅᎩᏘ ᏦᎦᏘᏂᏙ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎨᎲ Ᏺ ᏱᎩᎢᏓ Ꮲ ᎸᎯᏴ ᎦᏅᎩᏘ ᏦᎦᏘᏁᎦ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏍᎫᏭᏅ ᎣᎬᎵᏍᏕᏝᏙᏛ ᎡᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ ᏅᏬᏘ
segments.translation: And for colds there are several different things that I know of. Those red oak trees’ bark, boiled, is medicine, and also little sun, I was raised. No matter what’s going around, if they say there is a sickness going around, my dad would go all the way to the creek and look for that roots. Little sun and young kochunegi and tsuganvtsdi: those plants are sweet that are by the creek. Diganvsdi and another they call kanasutlawadi, you cut them up and put them together and wrap them with a string. Put them together and boil them. It’s good – they never took us to the doctor, that I will admit. I will admit they never took us to the doctor. That’s what we relied on: medicine from the woods.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎾᎭ ᎣᏴᏤᏂ ᏱᎦ Ꮭ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᏔ ᏅᏬᏘ, ᎣᏴᏤᏂ
segments.translation: What about for the throat? Do you know any medicine for the throat?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: What is it?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: He said “the throat.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏴᏤᎾ ᏝᎮ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᏔ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: The throat. Is there any medicine you know for that?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: For the throat, no I don’t think so.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏳᏅᏛᏭ Ꮄ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎤᎵᏏ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏯ ᎠᎩᏙᏓ ᎤᎵᏌ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏂᏓᏰᏥᎢᎸᏗ ᎠᏥᎢᎶᏢ ᎨᎮ ᎤᎷᏧ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎧᏃᎮᏢᏍᎬ ᎣᎩᏃᏎᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: She might have known, his grandma. My dad’s grandma was driven from North Carolina. When he came, he would tell us about what he talked about, the medicine.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: We'll I'll be!

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Medicine.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He must have known a lot of medicine ain't it.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ ᏍᏈᏍᏕ ᎤᏛ. ᏃᎴ Ꮕ ᎠᎾᏍᏋᏅᎪᎩ ᏣᎾᏗᏍᎪ Ꮎ ᎤᎦᏐᏃ ᎢᎩᎳᎥ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᏥᎦᏅᎪᎩ ᎥᎸᎯᏳᎮᏂ ᏴᏫ ᏍᎩ ᏂᏚᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁ ᏍᎩᏂ ᏣᎦᏔᎲ ᏅᏬᏘ. ᏳᏟᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎹ ᏯᎵᏟᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎳᏍᎩ ᏱᎬᏛᎩ boil ᏱᏂᎬᎩ Ꮎ ᎠᎹ ᎾᎾ roots Ꮓ ᏱᎧᏁᏐᎸᏍᏗ ᎤᎾᎦ ᎠᏄᏬ ᏯᏟᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᏓᏟᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏓᎵᏍᏕᏝᏙᏗᏍᎬᏂ. ᎪᎯᎾ ᏥᎦ ᏣᏁᎯ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ just anybody ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏣᏁ ᎯᏛ ᏱᏣᏗᏔᎭ ᎤᎤ ᎲᎥ ᏯᏅᏗ ᎠᏂᏁᎵᎰ. ᏃᎴᏂ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ ᏱᎦ ᏣᏁ ᎠᏯ ᏛᏲ ᏥᏣᎳᎩ Ꮭ ᏲᏁᎦᎭ ᏱᎦᏨᎵᏃᎮᏗ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎤᎾᏩ ᎠᏅᎬᏔᎭᏍᎪ
segments.translation: Yeah, he knew a lot and also what they call hemorrhoids. How the rectum goes down and comes out. Sometimes that happens to people. He knew medicine for that. He would have water in a kettle and boil the water and roots, and get out the particles with a white cloth. He would stop it. And now, these children that are living, just anybody’s kids here, if you tell them to drink this they will say “Ewww.” No, they don’t like it. And also, these children don’t talk Cherokee. I tell them, “I’m Cherokee, I can’t talk to y’all in English”. They just turn around.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᎾᎾ ᎧᎾᏍᏛᏟ, ᎧᎾᏍᏛᏟ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎬᏗ sasafrass ᏙᎭ
segments.translation: What about kvnastlvi? In English, it's Sassafras, ain't it?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Uh huh. [Yes].

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Isn't that...?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏣᏂᏍᎷᏍᎪ ᏍᎫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏓ ᎤᏩᏯᏢ ᎯᎠ Ꮲ ᏱᎩᏓ ᎠᏰᏟᏂ ᎤᎾᎦ ᎬᎸ ᏩᏂᎨ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎫ ᏓᏅᏓᎬᏚᏟᏍᎪ ᏍᎫ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏗᏂᎦᏙᎵ
segments.translation: They used to split a branch about ye big. In the center is white and soft. They used to splash it on the eyes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎧᎵᏤᏥᎾ, ᎧᎵᏤᏥ ᏣᏃᎮᎰ ᏧᏣᏲᏍᏗ ᏡᎪ ᏧᏣᏲᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᏒᎾ Ꮲ ᏧᏣᏲᏍᏗ ᏄᏍᏛᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏕᎯᎨᏩᏍᎬ
segments.translation: And, Sugar, [Honey Locust] they call the tree that has thorns. If you find a spot that has no thorns, that’s medicine for blindness.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, I have heard that.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That’s the Sugar tree? [Honey Locust]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Uh huh, yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏍ Ꮎ ᎤᏩᏛᎸᏗ ᎠᎵᏟᏙᏗ ᏗᎦᏚᏟᏍᏗ ᏙᎨ?
segments.translation: That sugar, do you boil the bark and put it in your eyes?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ, ᏍᏈᏍᏓ Ꮫ ᏧᏣᏲᏍᏗ ᏄᏍᏙ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎧᎵᏤᏣ ᎠᏃᏎᎰ ᏡᎦ Ꮂ ᏱᎦᏴᎦᏂ ᏗᎦᏅᎯᏓ ᏗᎦᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꭱ Ꭵ ᏙᏳ ᏍᏊ ᏍᏓᏯ ᎠᏩᏛᏗ ᏄᏍᏛᏂ ᏧᏣᏲᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᎲᏂ Ꮩ ᎤᏁᎦᎸᏭ ᏱᎦ ᏎᎦᏨ ᏴᏩᏘ ᎠᏩᏔᎾ ᏍᎫ ᏡᎦ Ꭿ ᏱᎩᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎸᏍᏄᏒᏭ ᎠᎩᎪᎲ ᎤᎾᏅ ᏡᎦ ᏨᎦᏙᎳ ᏅᏬᏔ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᏍᏗᏭᏂ ᏱᏣᏩᏛᎸᎭ ᏓᎶᏂᎨ ᏄᏍᏓ ᏩᏂᎨ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᏣᏍᏛᎪᏏ ᎠᏄᏬᏅ ᎤᎾᎦ ᏱᏣᏇᏂᏛᏂ ᏱᏗᏣᎧᏁᏟ ᏍᏓᏯ ᎠᎼ ᏱᏣᏟ ᏱᏔᎵᎦᏛᏟ ᏅᏬᏘ. I know that ᏛᏲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, that has lots of thorns. They call it sugar tree. You can’t grab it. They are real long. It’s really hard to find a spot that does not have thorns, that has just the skin. You can barely find it. I know where there is a tree this big, like that. I seen it the other day. “There is a tree for the eyes,” I thought. If you just take the bark off, a little bit its yellow, its soft and you scrape that, wrap it in a white cloth and tie it tight. Soak it in water and drop it in your eyes. It’s medicine – I know that about that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏅᎮᏂ eyedrop ᎠᏟᏍᏙᏗ ᏣᏟᏍᎬ ᎡᏘᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎩᎶ Ꮎ ᎠᏭ ᏥᏂᎬᏁᎲ
segments.translation: He used to put it in eye drop container a long time ago and he would just do it like this.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: And drop it in his eyes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, this is really medicine she's talking about.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎧᎵᏤᏥ Ꮎ ᎪᏍᏓᏯ ᏧᏍᏛᏂ ᏱᎦ ᏍᎩᎧ?
segments.translation: Sugar tree that doesn’t have the thorns, is that it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎧᎵᏤᏥ ᏄᎵᏍᏓᏁᎯᏱᎦ ᏥᏓᏂᎨᏩᎪ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏣᏅᏗᏍᎪ yeah ᏙᎲ ᎤᎪᏗ ᎯᎦᏔᎮ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏙᎭ?
segments.translation: They used to use that for blindness caused by diabetes. So you did know a lot of medicine, ain’t it. You were taught a lot.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: You’ve been taught a lot.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ ᎠᏓ ᏗᏓᎶᏂᎨ ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᏍᏊ ᏕᏥᏢ ᏕᏤᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏱᏣᏗᏔ ᏯᏑᎵᎪ
segments.translation: Yeah, and what they call yellow wood too, if your joints are hurting, you drink it. It will stop.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: We'll I'll be!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Is it a little bit like arthritis, is that it?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yes, arthritis?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Arthritis ain't it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What did she say the name of it is?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᏓᎶᏂᎨ ᎠᏓ ᏣᏗ ᏍᎩᏍ Ꮎ ᎦᎵᏣᏗ ᏥᏓᏃᏢᏗᎰ ᏍᏊ
segments.translation: That yellow wood you're talking about, is that what they make bows out of too, is that it?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: No, that’s locust, to make bows with.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Locust.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎧᎵᏣᏗ ᏛᏲ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᎮᏂ Ᏺ ᏱᎦᎪᏢᏂ
segments.translation: I can't make a bow.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [all laugh]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᎩᎦ ᎤᎾᎵᏒᎵᏓᏁᎲ Ꮂ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᏗ?
segments.translation: What about for high blood pressure, do you know anything?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎩᎦ ᎤᎾᎵᏒᎵᏓᏁᎲ Ꮟ. All I know Ꮕ ᏆᎶᎦ. ᏆᎶᎦ ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᏅᏃᎱᏟᏗ Ꮲ ᏥᏄᏍᏙ. ᏧᏭᏙ ᎩᎦᎨ ᏱᎬᏂ ᎤᏩᏂᏐᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎼ ᏱᎦᏢ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ Ᏺ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎨᎲ Ꮲ ᎠᏩᏁᎵᏢᏛᏅ ᏱᎦ. ᎠᏩᏅᏖᏲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: For high blood pressure, let me see. All I know is qwalogi, they call. It is usually on side of the road somewhere. When it ripens it will be a red berry. When it’s fully ripe, put it in water and they say that’s medicine. I have never tried it, but I do know that it is medicine.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Lillie, what about the one they call black?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That “Black” they call it.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: What medicine is that used for?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏧᎾᎸᏕᎯ ᎢᏛ ᎤᎾᏅᏬᏙᏗ ᎠᎹ ᎤᏂᏟᏍᏙ ᎤᎸᏒᏗ ᎤᎾ ᎦᏠ roots ᎠᎾᏗᏔᏅ pssss. ᏳᎾᏗᏩᏅ ᎠᏩᏅᏬᏛᏅᎾ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: That is for people that pass out to heal their self with. They will have water in a glass and have the roots in there and when they drink it, they blow it out and they are healed. I have healed myself with that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Really.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: It has happened to me and it helped me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I'll be.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎨ ᏳᎴᏅ ᎦᎵᏬᎬ ᏙᎮᏂ ᎬᏂᎨ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᏙᎭ? ᏔᎵ ᎮᏂ ᏓᏩᏘ ᎤᎾ ᏚᏰᎬ Ꮭ ᏍᎩᏂ Ᏺ ᏯᏩᏖ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏭᎪᏛ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎠᎬᏛᎦᏅ Ꭱ Ᏺ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: When that starts dying it really does turn black ain't it. I know two places where there are plants, but I didn’t know what it was mostly medicine for, but I have heard that it was.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎤᎪᏗ Ꮫ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎠᏰ ᏂᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᎢᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᎮᏂ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᏰᎦ
segments.translation: It is medicine for lots of things. What I think is everything is medicine that is planted.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎩ Ꭷ ᏱᎦ ᎢᎦᏞᏲᎯᏎᎵ ᏳᏗ ᏛᎮ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᎦᏙᎯᏍᏗ. ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᏂᏕᎦᏓᏂᎵ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ. ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎹ Ꮎ Ꮩ ᎦᏙ ᎭᏫᎾ ᏂᏓᏳᏛᎴᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎢᏓᏗᏔᏍᎬ ᎪᎯᏅ ᏥᎦ ᏥᏓᏗᏔᏍᎦ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎦᎷᎩ Ꮂ ᏱᎦᏯᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎤᏂᏑᏴ. ᎠᎹ Ꮽ ᏅᎮ ᏍᎫ ᏂᎨᎰ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎢᏓᏗᏔᏍᎨ ᎾᎯᏳ. Ꮩ ᎤᏁᎳᏅᎯ ᎤᏓᏁᏢᏅ
segments.translation: I guess you could say that kind of knowledge has become unfamiliar to us. That is why there is so much sickness. Back then we were drinking water that came from the ground and now days we drink the water that comes inside the house. There ain’t no telling what they have mixed in it. Even the water we were drinking back then had medicine in it. That God had provided.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎤᏁᎳᏅ Ꭱ ᎤᏓᏁᏢᏅ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏴᏫ ᎤᎵᏍᏕᏟᏙᏗ ᎤᏰᎨᏍᏗ ᎤᏪᎵᏎ ᎤᏓᎾᏖᏞ ᎤᏛᏎ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᏰᎪ ᏱᎪᎵᏥᎾ Ꮓ ᏯᏁᏟᏛᏂ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏴᎦᏎᎮᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏅᏬᏘ. ᎠᏎ ᎠᎩᏯᎴᎪ ᎨᎲ ᏫᏂᎬᏅᏕᏍᎪ ᎪᏢᏍᎬ it did help me. ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏩᏓᏙ ᎨᎲ. Ꮎ ᎮᏂ arthritis ᏣᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᏗᏛᎴᏍᎩ ᏣᏃᎮ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏯᏩᎵᏍᏓᏁ ᎠᏯ arthritis ᏯᎩᏁᏘᏍᏗ ᏓᏪᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎡᎯᎾ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᎫᏅ ᏣᎪᏗ ᎤᎦᏃᏩ ᎡᎳᏓ ᎥᎬᏓ ᏘᏅᎦᏟᏗ. ᏱᏙᎪᏘᏍᎦᏅ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏚᏬᏘᏒ ᎡᎳᏓ ᏱᏂᏕᎦᎵᏍᏛᏃᏂ. ᏍᎫ ᏭᎬᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᏕᏟᏙᏙ ᎠᏯ
segments.translation: I think God had provided the medicine helpful to man to have, when He thought about it. When that plant grew and when you recognize it and try it, when I was told about a medicine I would go look for it and get it and make it. It did help me. I would feel good. You said arthritis, that’s dedvlesgi, they call it. That is what I have, dedvlesgi, arthritis. If the pain gets unbearable, there is a medication for that. You do brew it, make it warm rub downward, clean it. If they are swollen, all the swelling will go down. That is mostly what is helpful to me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What is the name of that medicine?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏦᎵ Ꮫ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏃᏎᎰ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏘ. ᏧᎦᎶᎩ ᎮᏂ Ᏼ ᏂᏕᎩ. Ᏼ ᏱᏗᎦᏅᎯᏓ ᎤᏰᏍᏓᎣ ᏳᏍᏗ. ᎸᏢᏛᏴ ᏴᏪᏙᎵ ᏱᏥᏲᎩ
segments.translation: It looks like tobacco, they call it… I don’t know. The leaves are this big, this long. It kinda lays flat. If I come back again some day I will bring it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [unclear]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏙᏍ Ꮎ ᏦᎵ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎧᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ?
segments.translation: Does it really look like tobacco?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏳᏔᏏᏅ ᏎᎷ Ꮽ ᎡᎵᏍᏓ ᏩᎦᏍᏓᏓ ᎦᎸᎳᏗ
segments.translation: Yes, and when it grows, it has a head on top that looks like corn.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎠᎩᎪᎲ Ꮫ ᏍᏊ Ꮩ ᎨᎵ ᏙᎮᏂ ᏦᎳ Ꭴ ᎡᎵᏍᏓ ᏙᎭ Ꮎ ᏧᎦᎶᎩ ᏂᏚᏍᏗ ᏍᏙᎩᏗᎾ Ꮓ ᎡᎯ ᎮᏂ Ꮲ ᏃᏥᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᏍᎩᏍᎪ Ꮎ ᎠᎵᏟᏙᏗ ᏙᎨ?
segments.translation: I think I have seen it. It has leaves that really look like tobacco a little bit. It’s growing somewhere about this time ain't it? Do you boil that or what?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ ᎠᎼ ᏱᏣᏟᏍᏛᏂ pot ᏧᎳᏍᎩ ᏳᏦᏛᏂᏅ ᏳᏟᏢᎯ ᏯᏙᏢᏂ ᏍᎩᏃ ᎦᏓ ᎤᎵᏑᏴ ᎯᏅᏒᎴᏍᎬ ᏱᏣᏢᏂ ᎠᏄᏬ ᎤᎾᎦ ᎤᎾᏅ ᏱᏣᏟ ᎤᏙᎣᏢ ᏱᎦ ᎢᎾ ᎦᏓ ᏯᎲᎷᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎦ. ᎠᏗᏔᏍᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎦᏗᏔᏍᎪᏂ ᏍᏊ
segments.translation: Yes, just put water in a pot or kettle and build a fire and let it boil and the dirt that is mixed gets it out. Then, get a white cloth, lay it down, put it on there, let it soak and it will block most of the dirt. It’s good to drink. I drink it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏍ well ah be. Ꭰ ᏙᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᎾᎦ ᎠᏄᏬ ᏣᏗ? ᏙᎲ Ꮓ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎦᏙᏗ ᏥᎦ?
segments.translation: That white cloth you are talking about, why do you have to use that?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Oh, sheets?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᏙᎲ ᎤᏰᏟᏙ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎦᏅᎦᎵᏍᎩ ᎤᏭᎨ ᏱᎦ?
segments.translation: What's the reason for that? Does it clean it?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ ᏅᏅ ᎦᏓ ᎧᏁᏏᏢ ᎠᎭᎷᎩᏍᎦ. ᎠᏂᏅ ᏩᏟᎬ ᎤᏓᏅᎦᎸᏗ ᏱᎦ
segments.translation: Yes, it blocks the dirt particles from getting through. Then it pours in there, it will be clean.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: So you have to use a white cloth?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yes, white.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Why do you think you have to use that?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏍᎩᎾ ᏤᎵ ᎤᎾᎦ ᎥᏄᏬ ᎬᏙᏗ ᏱᎦ?
segments.translation: I wonder why you have to use a white cloth.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎠᏯ Ꮫ ᎨᎲ ᏂᎨᎵᏍᎬ ᎠᎩᎪᏛᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᎠᎷᎩᏍᎬ
segments.translation: The reason, I think, is so I can see what I am catching.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Dirt particles.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏲᏁᎩ Ꮎ ᎬᏗ filter ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᎭ
segments.translation: In English, it would be a filter, is what they would call it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: It’s catching it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎮᏂ ᏂᎪᎸ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏳᏂᏃᎮᏟ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎤᎾᎦ ᎥᏄᏬ ᎨᎰ ᏃᎴᏅ ᏃᎴ Ꮕ ᎤᎾᎦ ᎥᏄᏬ ᎦᏇᏂᏙᏗ ᎨᎰ Ꮎ ᎠᏟ ᎥᎲ ᎫᏍᏗ Ꮕ ᎤᏰᏟᏗ ᎢᎨᎵᏍᎪ
segments.translation: When they talk about medicine, they always say you have to use a white cloth and you also have wrap it in a white cloth. There must be some reason there. Must be some reason, I think.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎫᏍᏗ Ꮫ, ᏣᏅᏗᏍ ᏣᏅᏗᏍ ᎤᎪᏗ Ꭱ ᏱᏃᎵᏍᏓᏍ Ꮎ ᎪᏪᎵ ᎤᎲᎨᏙ ᎠᎩᏓ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ ᎤᏟᏴᎦᏛᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏚᎾᎳᏏᏙ. ᏢᏍ Ꮲ ᏱᏂᎬᏂ Ꮎ ᏉᎵ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᏁᎦ ᎥᏄᏬ ᏍᎫ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᏮᏛᏁ ᏙᎭ Ꮲ ᏥᏂᎬᎾ
segments.translation: You know, it will come to you. A lot of that has originated from the Bible and they stand on that is written. Paul used a white cloth, it’s written somewhere.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎫ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏚᎳᏏᏕ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎾᏩᎵᏍᏓᏏ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏂᏩ ᏧᏩᏮᏓᏖᏗ
segments.translation: He stood on that. That is how I felt when you said that. It gave me a thought.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, there was a reason.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: And mushrooms also.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏫᏌ, ᎤᎫᎫ, ᏩᏂᎯ ᎠᎾᎵᏍᏛᏍᎩ ᎤᏂᏠᎩ. ᎤᏂᏖᏗ
segments.translation: And mushrooms also. Wish, owl and hickory, chickens and slick heads.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They are delicious, oh, yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Oooh!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I couldn’t get enough if there is mushrooms on the table.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You wouldn’t?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [laughs]

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: You don’t hardly like them.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: I couldn’t get enough, I would eat till it runs out.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: I would eat them by their self.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That's right.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And wishie and…

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Those really are needed.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They are needed.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎯᎮᏃ ᎤᎵᎪᎲᏍᏗ ᏗᏝ ᏥᎦ ᏳᎦᏅᏂ. Ꮲ ᎮᏂ ᎡᎵᏍᏓ ᏳᏂᏍᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏩᏁᎢ ᎠᎾᎵᏍᏛᏍᎩ ᏙᎭ?
segments.translation: Now that it’s turning fall, if it rains, there should be some somewhere, those hickory chickens, ain’t it.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ ᏩᏁ ᏡᎦ Ꮲ ᏓᏩᏥᎵ ᎴᏱᎦ ᏓᏩᏥᎳ ᏡᎦ ᎤᏂᏍᏓᎣ ᏍᎫ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᏅ ᏩᏁᎢ ᎤᏂᎾᎩ
segments.translation: Yeah, if there is a hickory tree somewhere or an elm tree they will be on an elm tree too. On a hickory, they will be white.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏳᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᏲᎨᎲ ᏓᏬᎳ ᎠᎩᎸᏩᎦᏓ ᎠᏯ
segments.translation: I like any kind of mushrooms.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎪᎯᎦ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᏥ ᏣᎵᏏ ᎢᎾ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗᎢ ᏱᏧᏛᏂ. Ꭾ ᏱᏘᏯᏛᏛᏂᏍᎡ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏝᎲ ᏙᎭ ᎩᎶᏫᏛᏴ ᏱᏦᏟ. ᎪᎯᏴᏅ ᏥᎦ ᎠᏂᏫᎾ ᎠᎾᏘ ᏙᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏝᎯ ᏯᏅᏗ. ᏙᎭ
segments.translation: Long time ago, when your mom or your grandma said, “It’s time to eat,” you didn’t ask them what was on the table, did you? You would be sitting there real quick and now a days, young men and women will say, “What’s on the table?”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎾᎲ ᎠᎹ ᎪᏢᏛᏅ gravy ᎤᎪᏗ ᏅᎮ ᏣᎬ ᎨᎮ ᏙᎭ
segments.translation: Yeah, man. What about water gravy? You have probably ate a lot of it ain't it?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Ooh, yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It is good to eat.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎠᎹ ᎤᏛ ᏱᎦ ᎪᏢᏙᎰ gravy Ꮲ ᎤᏅᏗ
segments.translation: I just used water to make gravy, not milk.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That was good.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎠᏧᏥ ᎮᏂ ᎡᎯ Ᏼ ᏂᎦᏘ. ᏔᎵᏁ ᎥᎩᎵᏌ Ꭵ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏧᏅᏄᏂ ᏗᏁᏙᎲ ᏳᏭᏁᏙᎵ ᎠᏑᏍᏗ ᏅᎮ ᎨᎪᏢᎾᏁᎰ ᎠᎮ Ꮲ ᏳᎸᏫᎦᏓ ᎠᏗᎰ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᏂ grandma ᏥᎪᏢᏍᎪ ᏍᎩ ᏛᏲ ᎠᎩᎸᏩᎦᏓ. ᎠᎹ ᎪᏢᏛᏅ ᎠᏑᏍᏗ. ᏎᎷ ᎢᏏ Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᎪᏢᏛᏅ ᎠᏑᏍᏗ ᎠᎩᎸᏩᎦᏗ
segments.translation: There is a boy staying with me, this tall. He’s my great grandson. When he goes to visit his relatives, I guess they make gravy for them. He says he doesn’t like it. But he says he likes the way grandma makes it, with water. I also like gravy made from cornmeal.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏅᎾ ᏍᏊ bean ball ᏣᏃᏎᎰ ᏎᎷ ᏚᏯ Ꮕ ᏗᎩᎸᏫᎦᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏯ ᏕᏥᎦᎥᎷ ᏱᏛ ᎪᎢᎾ ᎤᏗᏝᎦ ᏳᏮᏥᏍᏚᏟᎦ ᏃᎴ ᎠᎹ ᏳᏮᏥᏍᏚᏟᎦ Ꮩ ᏍᎫ Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᎩᎶ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎪᏢᏍᎩ ᏱᎦ Ꮓ Ꭺ ᏕᎨᏒᏗᏒ
segments.translation: And what they call beanball corn and beans. I really like those. I will cut them up and splash hot grease on it and also I will splash salt on it. There is really not hardly anyone that makes those anymore these days.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꮧ ᏱᏥᎦᏔᎭ ᏯᏅᏗ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ Lillie biscuit ᎢᏍ ᏱᏕᎰᏢᏂ? ᎤᏂᏝᎾᎣ ᎤᏅᏂᏍᏛᏅ ᎤᏟᏍᏓᏭ ᎬᏂᏍᏙᏗ ᏧᏂᏝᎰ Walmart Ꭲ ᎤᏂᏝᎾᎣ ᎦᏚ ᎢᎾ ᎧᏂᎩᏓ ᏕᎦᏥᏲᏢᎾᏁᎰ biscuit ᏧᏂᎸᏫᎦᏓ ᎪᎢ ᏅᏍᏊ ᏗᎬᏂᏍᏛᎾ biscuit ᏗᎩᎸᏫᎦᏓ yeah
segments.translation: At the church they will say, “Lillie, will you make biscuits?” They will have things on the table, just fast cooked food they have at Walmart, they have on the table and no bread. I make them biscuits. They like them. I like biscuits fried in grease.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏙᏗᏥᎦᏘᏴ ᏲᎦᎵᏍᏓᏴᏂ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎠᏂᏅᏫᏍᏗᎰ ᎠᎦᏍᏓᏴᏍᎦ ᏚᏯ ᏧᏩᏂᏍᏙᏗ ᎥᎲ ᏄᏓᎴ Ꭱ ᎩᎶ ᏱᏓᏂᏲᎦ ᏚᏯ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮲ ᎰᏩ ᏱᏙᎬᏂᎦ ᎬᏂ ᎩᎳ ᎠᎦᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎩᎶᏭᏛᏴ ᎠᎵᏒᎲᏍᎪ ᏚᏯ
segments.translation: Where I pastor, when we eat they always ask my wife to cook beans. Someone else will bring beans, but they won’t hardly eat them unless it’s my wife, then we quickly run out of beans.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏚᏯ Ꭱ ᎤᏟ ᏳᏂᏖᏗ ᏳᏭᎾᏘ ᏫᏓᏙᏛᎾ ᏙᎭ ᏔᎵᏁ
segments.translation: Boy, beans are good if there is some left over, if you reheat them a second time.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: They are even better reheated.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: What's the name of the place you pastor?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Steely over by Kenwood.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Oh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᎵ Ꮫ ᏃᏭ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᎾᏕᏘᏱ ᏂᏗᏥᎦᏘᏲ Ꮎ
segments.translation: I have been their pastor there for a few years now.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏙᏍ? Ꭴ that’s good-- ᎣᏍᏓ Ꭷ. ᎡᎵ ᎨᏲ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᏂᏥᎣ?
segments.translation: Really? Ooh, that’s good. Is there quite a few of y'all there?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Sometimes.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Us too, sometimes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭ ᏃᎴ ᎡᎳᏓ ᏱᎦ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏃᎴ ᎣᎩᎪᏗ ᏱᎦ
segments.translation: Sometimes it'll be down and then sometimes there’ll be a lot of us.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Do they sing mostly in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, ᏓᏂᏃᎩᏍᎪ Ꭱ ᏳᏓᎭ ᏃᎴ ᎢᎦᏗ ᏳᏁᎦ Ꮎ ᎩᎳ ᏗᎾᏛᏍᎦ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏳᏁᎩ Ꮫ ᎾᏅ ᏧᏅᏛᎾᏯ ᏱᎦ ᏗᏣᎳᎩ ᏛᏃ ᎡᏧᎵᏛ ᏙᏣᏗᎰ
segments.translation: They sing, then sometimes in English. The young ones in English and the older ones in Cherokee. We use both.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: It's important.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꭳ yeah, ᏂᎾᎭ ᏅᏯ Ꮫ ᏗᏐᏴ ᏣᏗᎲ
segments.translation: Oh yeah. What about you, she said Rock Fence?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏅᏯ ᏗᏐᏴ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ Ꭸ ᏍᎫ ᏕᏥᏃᎩᏍᎪ?
segments.translation: At Rock Fence, do y'all sing in all Cherokee?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: They don’t sing in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They don't, well I'll be.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ ᏦᏍᏛᏓᎸ ᎠᏩᏓᏠᎩᏴᏅ ᏐᎢᎾ my cousin Terry Bird ᏗᏂᏙᎾᎣ Ꮲ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᏣᎳᎩ ᏱᏗᎦᏃᎩᏍᎪ ᎤᏂᏑᎵᎪᏦᏂ. ᏙᎲ ᏥᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ Ꮕ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᏣᎳᎩ Ꮕ ᏂᏓᏂᏃᎩᏍᎬᎾ ᏥᎦᏥᏲ ᎮᎲ. Ꮧ ᏱᏙᏥᎦᏔᎭ ᏯᏅᏗ
segments.translation: That’s what I tell them, my sister my niece and my other cousin Terry Bird. They stand up there and nobody sings Cherokee. They have all stopped. I asked them why. “This is a Cherokee church and there’s no Cherokee singing,” I told them. “We don’t know any,” they will say.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎾᎲ ᎢᏥᎦᏘ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ Ꭸ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏑᏴᏴᏍᎪ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎬ?
segments.translation: What about y’alls pastor? Does he mix Cherokee into his preaching?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yes, he does, the one that’s here that’s a Flute?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, uh huh.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: He’s does it all in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The older one.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: One verse ᏳᎪᎵᏰ Ꮎ Bible ᏣᎳᎩ ᏂᎬᏁᎰ Ꭴ ᎠᎩᎸᏩᎦᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏯ
segments.translation: Yes, he does, the one that’s here that’s fluent in Cherokee. When he reads one verse, then he puts it in Cherokee oooh, I really like that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏛ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎫ ᏙᏗᏥᎦᏘᏴ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏁᎵ ᎠᏎ ᎠᏣᎳᎦ ᎠᎦᏑᏴᏓ ᎨᎰ ᏯᏩᎵᏥᏗᏂ ᎭᎸᎯᏳ ᎮᏂ ᎩᎶ ᎣᎩᏩᏛᎯᏙ ᏳᏪᏙᎵ boy ᏥᎸᏬᏓ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏣᏑᏴᏂᏙᎭ ᏯᏗᏛ ᏙᎮᏂ ᏣᏗ ᎢᎦᏗ ᏙᎮᏂ ᏝᏙ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏯᎾᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎪ ᏲᏁᎩ ᎭᏩ ᏱᎦ ᎮᎾ ᏣᏗ ᎤᎾᏠᎪ ᎮᏂ
segments.translation: Really, where I pastor there are some that are a little older and I have to mix in Cherokee when I preach. Sometimes when someone comes to visit, they will say I really enjoyed you mixing in Cherokee. Like you said, some don’t really preach in Cherokee, just in English and like you said, they miss it.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᏘᏴ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎦᏅᏛᏗᏍᎪ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏃᎴ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏳᎵᏥᏙᏂ ᏥᏓᏂᏃᎩᏍᎪ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎾᏅᏁᎲ ᎠᎾᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎬ yeah ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏢᏙ Ꮓ ᎰᏩ ᏰᎯ Ꮓ. ᎠᏎᎾ ᎠᏛᏁᏟᏴ ᏛᏃ
segments.translation: Long time ago, it was all in Cherokee. I remember, the preacher was Cherokee and when they preached they made it sound like they were singing. That’s not hardly around anymore but I guess it’s changing now.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: Ꭵ ᎤᎾᎵᏒᏂ ᏍᎫ Ꮩ ᎠᏂᎬᎵ ᎠᎾᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᏝᏅ ᏴᏁᎯ
segments.translation: Yeah, they have ran out. Here is not any old preachers now.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That’s where we are standing now.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Can you read in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Can you read Cherokee?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏢᏙ ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᏍᎪ, ᏢᏛ ᎩᎶ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᎢᎾ ᏰᎯ ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏲᏁᎦ, ᏲᏁᎦ Ꮭ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏓᎩᏂ ᎢᎾ ᏍᏊ ᏗᏣᎳᎩ ᎪᏪᎵ bible ᏫᏗᏥᎦᏃ Ꮫ ᎠᏬᏠ ᏙᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏗ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ
segments.translation: Not really, I can’t seem to do. There ain’t no teacher there. English, English, English, no Cherokee. I have some Cherokee Bibles too. I will be sitting there, looking, thinking, “What’s he saying?”

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: Guy, you can read Cherokee ain't it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, I can read some of it, yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏣᏥ ᏥᎨ ᏣᏙᏗᏅ ᎠᏂᎦᏔᎮ ᎨᏲ. ᎤᏂᎪᎵᏰᏗ ᎠᏂᎦᏔᎮᏍ? ᏣᏥ ᏣᏙᏗᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ? ᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᏯᏂᎦᏔᎮ
segments.translation: What about your mom and dad? Did they know how to read Cherokee? Did they know how, your mom and dad? So, they didn’t know how either.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: My dad didn’t go to church.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎤᏂᎪᏗ Ꮟ ᏃᏥᎦ. ᏭᏂᎪᏛ ᏛᎮ Ꮭ church ᎠᏁᏙ ᏱᎦ ᏴᏫ
segments.translation: There is a lot still, most of the people don’t go to church.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No, they don't.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: I tell them, “That event y’all are having doesn’t last long.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yes, it does.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: They will know what I have told them, I think.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, ᏙᏛ ᎤᏲᏟ ᎮᏂ ᎢᏕᏙ ᏙᎭ Ꮓ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ. Ꮲ ᎩᎶ ᏳᏚᎵᎰ ᏱᏂᎬᏩᏍᏙ
segments.translation: Yes, it's true. We are in some bad times now days. Nobody seems to want to.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᎰᏩ ᏳᏚᎵ ᏂᎬᏩᏍᏙ ᏧᎳᏫᏥᏓᏍᏗ Ꮓ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎦ
segments.translation: Nobody seems to want to go to church now days.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: No. No.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᎴ ᏍᎫ ᎦᏚᎦ ᏥᏓᏗᎰ ᏥᏓᏗᎰ ᏝᏍᏊ Ꮓ ᎰᏩ ᏰᎯ Ꮓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏴᏛᏂ ᎡᏘᏴ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎩᎶ ᏱᏧᏓᏂᎳ ᏣᏁᎪ ᏧᏩᏂᏍᏕᎸᎯᏙᎰ ᏝᎦ
segments.translation: And also, we say togetherness, that doesn’t exist anymore. For instance, long time ago when someone was sick, they would go and help them for awhile.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎤᎵᏧᏛᏩᏗᏅ ᎠᏂᏃ ᏍᎫ ᏥᎨᎲ, ᎠᏂᎦᏘᏴ. ᎪᎯᏅ ᏥᎦ Ꮲ ᏍᎫ ᏱᎬᏂᏩᏛᎱᎦ ᎩᎶ. ᏴᏅᏛᏛᎲᏍᎩᎾᎠ
segments.translation: They would sit there all night waiting on them. Now days they won't even go visit anybody. They will just be asking about them.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏳᏩᏅᏓᏍ ᎤᏛ ᎤᏟᏍᏓ ᏙᎭ ᎣᏏᏭᏧ ᎥᎥ ᏂᎾ ᎥᎥ ᏙᏅᏓᎪᎲ ᏗᎾ
segments.translation: They will just call them real quick and say, “Are you ok?” “Yes, I am.” “Ok. See you again.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [all laugh]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᏅᏓᎪᎲᎢ ᏥᏓᏗᎰ ᎭᏂ ᏱᏗᏓᏓᎪᏩᏘᏍᎪ. ᎾᎾᎭ ᎭᏅᏛᏗᏍᎪ Ꭸ ᎩᎶ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᏧᏕᏂᏙᎸ ᏣᏂᏒᏍᏗᎲ. ᎭᏛᏛᏗᎰᏍ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: When we say, “I will see you again,” we don’t even see each other. Do you remember when someone passed away, they used to have a wake sevice where they used to live? Do you remember that?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᏂᎪᏗ ᏥᏓᏂᎷᎪ ᏙᏯ ᏗᏝ ᏃᎴ ᏣᏂᏙᎾᎣ ᏧᏃᏙ ᏙᏛᎭᏃ
segments.translation: A lot would come. They would be standing outside and have a fire built.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏍᏊ ᎢᎾ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎦ ᏍᎫ ᎤᏓᏁᏟᏴᏏ
segments.translation: Even that has changed.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏃᎴ ᎤᏓᏂᎴ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᎦ ᏯᎾᏓ. ᎬᏬᏂᏍᎬᏩ Ꭱ ᏴᏫ ᎠᏩᏛᎲᏍᏗ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ Ꮲ ᏄᏛᏂ. ᎠᎩᏩᏛᎰᎩ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏰᎵ ᎮᏂ ᏳᏓᎪ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᏳᏲᎱᏏᏅ Ꮓ ᎠᏲᎱᎯ ᏃᏫᏛ ᎦᏟᎩ ᏯᏁᏂ
segments.translation: And also, they will say, “That one is sick. He is in bed.” I told them you need to visit someone while they still can speak. Not when he doesn’t know. He will think that one came to visit me. And when they pass away, they will say he passed away, then a group will go. There use to be a man named Gvligeni/Buck Seabolt.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, yeah.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᎦᎳᎩᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏧᏙᎩᏗ ᏤᎲ buck seabolt. Ꮑ Ꮎ ᏧᏂᏲᎱᏒ ᏗᏂᏰᏍᎩ ᏛᎾᎢ ᏯᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏥᏝᏫᏍᏛᏂ ᏎᎵ ᏧᏙᎩᏓ ᎠᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᎤᎤᎤ ᏱᏣᏪᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᎲᏂ ᏂᏪᎠ ᎠᎪᏎᎲ ᏙᏗᎲ Ꮭ ᎡᏍᎦ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏓᏁᎮ
segments.translation: “Look, those people that eat the dead are coming,” he would say. I used to live with an old lady named Sali. She would tell him, “Woo, you are saying something you should not say”. It’s true he didn’t feel bad about it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᏍᎪᏂ ᎠᏗᎮ ᎩᎳ ᏳᏲᎱᏏ ᎩᎳ ᏣᏂᎷᎪ
segments.translation: Was he talking about when someone passes away, then they come over?

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Really is.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᎤᏂᎨᏳ ᏥᎨᏐ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᎩᎶ ᏃᏛ ᎤᏂᎨᏳ ᎨᏐ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᎩᎶ ᏃᏛ ᎤᏂᎨᏳ ᎨᏐ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᏧᏩᎬᏛᏅᏒ ᎠᏂᎾᏩᏘᏍᎩ ᎨᏒᎬ
segments.translation: That’s when they really love them, when someone passes away, and in the past, they hated them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [all laugh]

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎠᎩᏚᏥ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏍᏭᎤ ᏥᏄᏪᏒ ᎦᏅᏛᏗᏍᎪ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏦᏍᏛᏛᏁᎲ ᏥᏥᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᎠᎩᏲᏎ ᎨᏃᏂ ᏧᏛᏅ ᏥᏲᎤᏒᏂ ᎩᎳ ᏓᎠᏂᏲᏢᏂ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎤᎬᎻ ᏂᎨᏐ ᏧᏛᏅ ᏣᏗᏍ ᏣᏗᏍ Ꮮ ᏍᎫ ᏑᏂᏙᏛᏩᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᎲᏂ ᎤᏓᏛ ᏧᏩᏂᎸ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ. Ꮩ Ꭱ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᎾ. ᏙᏳ ᏄᏪᏒ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎩᎳ ᏴᏫ ᏧᏂᎷᏨ ᏣᏂᏲᎯᎲ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᏧᏩᏩᏛᏛ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏪᏒ. ᏙᎮᏂ
segments.translation: I remember what my uncle said, he said, “I am really hungry. When I pass away, then they are going to be bringing food like soup.” You know, it wasn’t a week he had a heart attack and he passed away. Really that’s what happened. Really, what he said happened. People were coming and bringing food. I remembered what he said. It’s true.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎮᏂ ᏗᎨᎬ ᏍᏭ ᎤᏔᎾᏯ Ꮕ ᎩᎶ ᏧᏂᏒᏛᏅ ᏧᏪᏅᏒ. ᎾᏅ ᏳᏪᏙᎵ ᎤᏛᏅ ᎡᎵᏅ ᏲᏛᏍᏓᎾᏏ. ᎮᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᏱᏛᏂᏯ ᏛᏂᏂᏌᏂ ᎮᏂ ᏣᎪᏎᎸ
segments.translation: Where I come from there is an elder. They had a wake service at their house. They said if you go over there you could get something to eat. He said they are not going to eat them, they are going to bury them

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: [all laugh]

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏱᏛᏂᏯ ᎤᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎡᎵᏍᏓ Ꮩ ᏂᎬᏪᏍᎨ
segments.translation: He did make it sound like they were going to eat them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, yeah. ᏙᎮᏂ ᏣᏗ ᎯᎾ ᏍᏈᏍᏓ ᏯᏂᏲᏢᎩ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᏤᎲᏂᏭ ᎠᎪᏂ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏄᏛᏁ ᏃᏅ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏁ ᏣᏗ ᏃᎴ ᎤᎪᏗ ᏯᏂᏲᏢᎩ. ᎩᎶ Ꮕ ᏯᎪ ᏄᎲᏂᏅ ᏱᎦ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎾᎯᏳᏭ Ꮕ ᏩᏲᎯᏍᏗ ᏙᎭ ᎬᏃᏗ ᎨᏒ ᏙᎭ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎦ ᏥᏲᎱᏒ Ꮫ ᎠᏗᎲ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏧᎾᏥᎸᏍᎩ ᏗᏣᏩᏒᎢ ᎠᏬᏎᎲ ᎬᏃᏚᏭ ᎨᎲ ᏕᏍᎩᏅᏁᎮᏍᏗ ᏧᎾᏥᎸᏍᎩ ᎠᏬᏎᎲ. ᏙᏛᎭ ᏍᏊ ᏙᎭ ᏢᏅ ᏛᎬᎪᏩᏗ ᎬᏁᏌᎢ ᏱᎦᎳ ᏧᎾᏥᎸᏍᎩ ᏓᏂᏃᎯᎲ yeah
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah. It’s true what this one said. They will bring lots of food. When they were alive, they may have been hungry, but when they pass away, they will bring a lot. If you see someone and they don’t have any food, you should just take it then, ain’t it, while they are still alive ain’t it. And also, my wife said when she passes away, she told me not to buy flowers, “Give me flowers while I am alive.” I guess it’s true. She can’t see them when she is in the box, that they are bringing flowers.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.text: ᏃᎴ Ꮕ ᎤᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩ ᏥᏓᏂᏢᏍᎩ ᏓᏓᏂᏌᎲ ᎢᎦᏓ. ᏩᏙ ᎠᎾᏓ Ꮷ ᏯᏅᏗ? ᏳᏓᏢᏂ
segments.translation: Also, when they put flowers on graves, some will say, “Did they say, ‘thank you’ when you lay them on there?”

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: That is just the shell of the person, ain't it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎤᏠᏱ ᏣᏗ ᎦᏓ ᏭᏅ ᏫᎾᏛᎦᎵᏍᏛᏂ. ᏙᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎾᏓᏗᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏴᏫ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏙᎭ
segments.translation: Just like it says they are going to return to dirt. The real memory of a person is here ain't it, is stored in the heart.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: [gesture to heart]

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᎴ ᎤᎪᏗ ᏱᏓᎾᏈᏱ ᏧᎾᏥᎸᏍᎬ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎩᎳ ᏱᏓᏂᏲᎯ ᏙᏅᎭ ᏤᎲ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏅᏛᏁᏗ ᎨᏎ ᏙᎭ. ᎭᎳ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ Ꮟ ᎤᏓᎷᎳ?
segments.translation: And also they will pay a lot of money for flowers. They will bring them then. It should have been done when they were alive. How much time is left?

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.translation: The time has came. It's been an hour.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I appreciate the conversation.

segments.speaker: lillie-vann
segments.translation: Me too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That really was a lot.
